questionText:
‘When the teacher is in the room, all students stand silently.’

If the above statement is true, which one of the following statements is not necessarily true?
options: If any student is not standing silently, then the teacher is not in the room.
When the teacher is in the room, all students are silent.
If all students are standing, then the teacher is in the room.
When the teacher is in the room, all students are standing.
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the given condition
Let $P$ = 'Teacher is in the room' and $Q$ = 'All students stand silently' (which means every student is both standing and silent).
The given statement is $P \implies Q$.

Step 2: Evaluate the options
• Option (A): Represents the contrapositive $\neg Q \implies \neg P$ ('If any student is not standing silently, then the teacher is not in the room'). A statement and its contrapositive are logically equivalent, so this is always true.
• Option (B): If all students stand silently, then they are all silent. Thus, when $P$ is true, all students are silent (must be true).
• Option (D): If all students stand silently, then they are all standing. Thus, when $P$ is true, all students are standing (must be true).
• Option (C): States 'If all students are standing, then the teacher is in the room.' This is the fallacy of affirming the consequent ($Q \implies P$). Students could be standing for another reason even if the teacher is not in the room.

Therefore, Option (C) is not necessarily true.
